nodes.name: Render driver
nodes.responsibility: Coordinates the current passes
nodes.description: Current paintArchitecture orchestrates relieveCongestion, route painting, label settlement, card painting and atlas creation. This sequence groups those helper calls by responsibility; it is not a new runtime module.

nodes.name: Card text
nodes.responsibility: Fits words into allocated space
nodes.description: Current fittedSize measures title widths and reduces type size to its floor. SVG card painting then applies measured ellipsis to titles and single-line responsibilities. The existing font measurement engine remains authoritative.

nodes.name: Grid placement
nodes.responsibility: Assigns fixed seats and rows
nodes.description: Current layoutArchitecture uses region bands, global rows and paired seats. cardHeight is46 or58 units depending on responsibility presence. Card text does not grow the card; title size fits the available width.

nodes.name: Route planning
nodes.responsibility: Plans indexed corridors and ports
nodes.description: Current relieveCongestion counts planned channel traffic and expands gaps before final routeEdges. Routes use grid bands/corridors. Label settlement happens later in paintEdges, before marks are emitted.

nodes.name: SVG marks
nodes.responsibility: Fits and paints the final marks
nodes.description: Current paintCard truncates title and responsibility using real font metrics. The architecture painter also settles edge-label boxes, emits marks and derives atlas bounds from actual geometry.

flows.name: Today: fit text after choosing seats

steps.label: Place regions in fixed seats
Fit title to available width
Measured fitted title size
Grid, card boxes and containers
Count traffic in indexed gaps
Channel traffic and label demand
Repeat placement if gaps need air
Allocate ports and route edges
Curved paths and label anchors
Settle labels on routed paths
Paint cards and relationships
Ellipsize title and responsibility
Painted SVG marks
Derive atlas from final drawn bounds

beats.heading: Fixed space comes first
beats.body: The grid chooses card space. Text fitting reduces the title size, and painting may still ellipsize it. Responsibilities remain one line. This is the behavior the proposal replaces.

beats.heading: Routing and labels follow placement
beats.body: Congestion relief can expand grid gaps and repeat placement. Final routes are produced after that; label boxes are settled in the architecture paint orchestration. The existing renderer already returns SVG and matching atlas bounds.

nodes.name: View dispatcher
nodes.responsibility: Measures, settles and paints one drawing, in that order
nodes.description: The renderer's entry point, drawn here only as the caller of the layout. Follow it for the rest of the renderer.

nodes.name: Measured text
nodes.responsibility: Wraps every card, note and label and measures what the SVG will paint

nodes.name: Compound layout
nodes.responsibility: Settles cards, frames, routes and labels as one drawing, and keeps a column fold only when it fits the pane better
nodes.description: Nothing after it may repair a coordinate. Every variant is laid out fresh (ADR 0032): one downward drawing first, then each column count that could fit the reference pane at least WRAP_MIN_FIT_GAIN better, keeping the best complete one. Crossings are bridged here, as geometry the reader sees.

nodes.name: Architecture painter
nodes.responsibility: Paints the settled drawing and decides no geometry of its own

nodes.name: Pretext
nodes.responsibility: Breaks a prepared string into lines at a given width

nodes.name: Host canvas
nodes.responsibility: The canvas of whatever draws the picture, with the diagram faces loaded
nodes.description: An @napi-rs/canvas canvas installed as OffscreenCanvas under Bun, the tab's own canvas in a browser. Both the line breaking and the painted runs are measured through it, so a line and its words agree (TASK-247).

nodes.name: Compound graph
nodes.responsibility: States containment, measured sizes, authored order, relationship kinds and comparison standing as one graph

nodes.name: Layout engine
nodes.responsibility: Places, folds and routes one graph inside a layout worker
nodes.description: createLayoutEngine binds the initialized Graphviz and libavoid WebAssembly engines. The host runs it in a worker pool: Bun Workers under Bun, Web Workers in a tab (layout-worker.ts). Engine coordinates are never authored or persisted (ADR 0033).

nodes.name: Column folds
nodes.responsibility: Names the column counts a settled drawing could fold into, and folds a placement into that many columns
nodes.description: Every board reads top to bottom (ADR 0033). A fold is a candidate the compound layout keeps only when it fits the reference pane materially better, fewer columns winning a tie. Nobody authors it, and a proposal is laid out fresh like any variant (ADR 0032).

nodes.name: Label reservations
nodes.responsibility: Reserves layout space for a label no run of its route can hold, and releases reservations a label no longer uses

nodes.name: Graphviz placement
nodes.responsibility: Places cards and frames with Graphviz's ranking across clusters, keeping containment

nodes.name: Obstacle routing
nodes.responsibility: Routes every relationship orthogonally around cards and unrelated frames, through shared ports per relationship kind
nodes.description: A relationship enters a container only when the container holds one of its ends; other frames are obstacles. The router chooses each end's face; one refinement from the settled paths is kept when it routes (ADR 0033).

nodes.name: Graphviz
nodes.responsibility: Ranks a clustered graph and places its nodes
nodes.description: @viz-js/viz: Graphviz compiled to WebAssembly, loaded by the layout worker.

nodes.name: libavoid
nodes.responsibility: Routes orthogonal connectors around obstacle shapes
nodes.description: libavoid-js, patched, compiled to WebAssembly and loaded by the layout worker.

beats.heading: Words first, then space
beats.body: Nothing is placed before it is measured. The size a name needs is a fact the layout is handed, in the face the SVG will paint, so no later pass has to make room it did not reserve.

beats.heading: Pretext breaks lines; the renderer owns card policy
beats.body: Pretext is given a prepared string and a width and hands back lines. Padding, icon space, baselines and the bounds a card may take are the renderer's, not the library's.

beats.heading: One owner places and routes
beats.body: Graphviz places the cards and frames, libavoid routes every relationship around them, and the labels settle on those routes, all under one owner. Nothing after it may repair a coordinate, which is why there is no second geometry to keep in step.

beats.heading: Every board reads down; a fold must earn its place
beats.body: Every variant is laid out fresh and reads top to bottom. A settled drawing folds into more columns only when that fits the reference pane materially better, and fewer columns win a tie. Nobody authors the reading.

beats.heading: The painter decides no geometry
beats.body: By the time the painter runs, every box, port, route and label box is settled. It paints what it is given, so the picture a reader points at and the atlas the inspector reads are the same geometry.

Then the page is cut to what it draws and crossings are bridged, as geometry the reader sees. Nothing after it may repair a coordinate.

nodes.name: Block placement
nodes.responsibility: Lays every block out innermost first, then puts each where its parent placed it
nodes.description: A block's size is final before its parent places it as one box. A block of cards may wrap its widest rank into rows or fold its ranks into columns where that reads better; last, each relationship's lines are joined end to end.

nodes.name: Card blocks
nodes.responsibility: Ranks a block's cards, labels and ports with Graphviz, then routes its lines on tracks between the ranks
nodes.description: Each channel between ranks grows to fit its tracks, so the block's size is final when it answers. Graphviz is asked once for each graph a layout gives it (graphviz-once.ts), and its answer is read into diagram coordinates by track/graphviz.ts.

nodes.name: Block packing
nodes.responsibility: Packs a block of blocks in rows or columns, whichever scores best on fit, crossings and detours

nodes.name: Trunk router
nodes.responsibility: Routes each trunk between two blocks' ports around the blocks it packs

beats.heading: Words first, then space
beats.body: Nothing is placed before it is measured. The size a name needs is a fact the layout is handed, in the face the SVG will paint, so no later pass has to make room it did not reserve.

beats.heading: Pretext breaks lines; the renderer owns card policy
beats.body: Pretext is given a prepared string and a width and hands back lines. Padding, icon space, baselines and the bounds a card may take are the renderer's, not the library's.

beats.heading: One engine places and routes
beats.body: Track or Blocks lays the board out, one block at a time from the innermost. Graphviz ranks a block's cards and its lines run on tracks between the ranks; libavoid routes the trunks between packed blocks. Nothing after it may repair a coordinate, which is why there is no second geometry to keep in step.

beats.heading: The drawing that reads best is kept
beats.body: A board is solved more than one way, and the answers are weighed as drawn: crossings, line length and how well it fits the reference pane, which is as wide as the shell gives a drawing and as tall as the tuned 1.4 page shape makes that width, not the shell's own pane (ADR 0043). A block of cards wraps a wide rank or folds tall ranks into columns only where that reads better. Nobody authors the reading, and every variant is laid out fresh.

beats.heading: The painter decides no geometry
beats.body: By the time the painter runs, every box, port, route and label box is settled. It paints what it is given, so the picture a reader points at and the atlas the inspector reads are the same geometry.
